title: Exact shared-SRAM read-group adapter frontier
hypothesis: The 512-bit two-slot adapter minimizes exact read-group service latency and its vectorless total-energy proxy at modest area cost, while the 512-bit one-slot adapter remains the minimum-area point.

direct_comparison.primary_question: Which embodied adapter width and slot count best serves the shared-SRAM read path before scheduler, endpoint, NoC, and macro costs are composed?
include: actual Icarus replay of all four generated RTL variants
cycle-model agreement for requests, macro reads, responses, stalls, folded output, and protocol status
common 2 ns timing-feasible Nangate45 instance area and vectorless total power
exclude: SRAM bitcell area and CACTI access energy

required_evaluations.objective: Verify all four adapter RTL traces against the cycle model and recost their local service frontier from merged physical evidence.

expected_result.reason: Replace width/slot throughput assumptions with RTL-exact cycle counts and common-clock physical metrics.

remaining_abstractions_after_this_step: SRAM capacity and access energy remain registry-composed.
Scheduler, packet endpoint, and NoC contention must be composed before selecting a Llama7B system point.
Vectorless power remains a screening proxy until workload activity is propagated.
